strings.name: Arundhati Roy
strings.summary: Writing in English, Roy moved from architectural studies and screenwriting to fiction and political essays. After The God of Small Things won the Booker Prize, she wrote extensively on nuclear weapons, dams, land and social inequality, returning to the novel twenty years later. Her public positions have provoked vigorous debate. Her writing links private lives with institutional power, while her 2025 memoir examines her relationship with her mother.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through September 2025; the education entry uses decade precision for the 1970s. Sources checked on 13 November 2026.
strings.influence.rationale: She has made an international impact through novels such as The God of Small Things and nonfiction, continually discussing class, land and social inequality.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Architectural studies at the School of Planning and Architecture, New Delhi
strings.highlights.h1.title: Booker Prize fiction
strings.highlights.h1.text: The God of Small Things won the 1997 Booker Prize, exploring caste and social boundaries through a family story.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Sustained public writing
strings.highlights.h2.text: Her political essays examine nuclear policy, dam development and costs borne by marginalized communities.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Publishes a memoir about her mother
strings.timeline.t1.text: Following publication of Mother Mary Comes to Me, she discussed her complex relationship with Mary Roy in interviews.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Receives the PEN Pinter Prize
strings.timeline.t2.text: English PEN awarded her the PEN Pinter Prize, recognizing her writing and sustained attention to injustice.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Publishes her second novel
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Ministry of Utmost Happiness appeared and was longlisted for the Booker Prize, interweaving the lives of marginalized characters.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Critiques large dam development
strings.timeline.t4.text: The Greater Common Good questioned the Narmada dam project, focusing on displacement and the costs of development.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Writes against nuclear testing
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published The End of Imagination after India’s nuclear tests, bringing criticism of nuclear weapons policy into her public writing.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Debut wins the Booker Prize
strings.timeline.t6.text: The God of Small Things won the Booker Prize and reached a wide international readership.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Writes and acts for film
strings.timeline.t7.text: Wrote and appeared in In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones, drawing on the lives of architecture students.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Studies architecture in Delhi
strings.timeline.t8.text: As a young woman she studied architecture in Delhi, later entering film before turning increasingly to literature.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Born in Shillong
strings.timeline.t9.text: Born in Shillong in northeastern India, she spent much of her childhood in Kerala, raised by her mother.
